title: Kimsuky Moves AI-Assisted Development Into Local Environment With Operation GitPower
content_md: North Korean threat actor Kimsuky has expanded its cyber espionage toolkit with local artificial intelligence tools as part of a campaign researchers call Operation GitPower. The activity combines the group’s familiar spear-phishing methods, malicious Windows shortcut files, PowerShell loaders, and GitHub-based command-and-control infrastructure with a growing AI development environment. Researchers at Genians Security Center found signs that Kimsuky is not simply testing public generative AI services. Instead, the group appears to be building local systems that can run large language models, process private documents, support code development, and convert speech to text without sending data to external providers. The campaign shows how established threat actors may use AI to improve operational speed while keeping their core intrusion methods unchanged. Kimsuky still relies on targeted social engineering and cloud-hosted infrastructure, but AI could help it create better lures, modify malware faster, and process stolen intelligence more efficiently. Kimsuky Launches Operation GitPower Operation GitPower begins with targeted spear-phishing emails carrying ZIP archives . These archives contain malicious LNK files disguised as legitimate documents. The lures use themes linked to government agencies, embassies, research, finance, legal agreements, and international events.
